paragraph: Matched learning rates (post hoc). B-H2 compared HQ at 3 × 10⁻³ with its twin at 10⁻³. After the B2 results were known, and under an analysis plan written before the runs, each pairing was therefore repeated at a common learning rate: the twin was re-trained at HQ's 3 × 10⁻³ and HQ at the twin's 10⁻³, on the same 36 blocks, each new run paired with the stored B2 run of the other arm, which shares its initialisation, training schedule and evaluation episodes. HQ − twin AUC was −0.0101 [−0.0133, −0.0068] at 3 × 10⁻³ (two-sided p = 2.9 × 10⁻⁷; HQ lower in 94% of blocks), and −0.0133 [−0.0178, −0.0089] at 10⁻³ (p = 6.0 × 10⁻⁷; 92%) (Table 11); both null hypotheses were rejected after Holm adjustment over the two contrasts at familywise 0.05. A machine crash interrupted the launch once; the 12 runs then in progress were restarted from the beginning, with the same seeds, under a rule written before the restart. At both matched learning rates HQ learned less than its exact twin, so the B-H2 difference is not explained by the learning-rate difference. Descriptively, raising the learning rate from 10⁻³ to 3 × 10⁻³ changed HQ's own AUC by +0.0055 [+0.0033, +0.0078] and the twin's by +0.0023 [−0.0019, +0.0065], and mean final-checkpoint weighted J was 0.023 (HQ) and 0.038 (twin) at 3 × 10⁻³, and 0.020 and 0.035 at 10⁻³.
conclusion: In paired early training, HQ has lower learning-curve area than C-matched and than its exact twin; a post-hoc check at matched learning rates leaves the HQ–twin difference in place.
abstract_clause: and than its exact twin, also at matched learning rates
